context: Wilde to George Ives, [circa 30 June 1894], New Travellers Club, Piccadilly. Ives was living at the Albany; the 'young Domitian' is unidentified.
quote: Dear George, I am charmed to see you are at the Albany — I am off to the country till Monday. I have said I am going to Cambridge to see you — but I am really going to see the young Domitian, who has taken to poetry! Next week let us meet. Yours
original_provenance: Read at HRC MSS_WildeO_2_7_019 and _020, two sides on New Travellers Club paper; the envelope to Ives at the same club is _021-_022. Emphasis: none - nothing is underlined on either side, a null finding. Punctuation: two dashes restored, each written hard after the word it follows and reading as his punctuation - 'at the Albany — I am off', where the printed text has a full stop, and 'to see you — but', where it has a comma. Not resolved: the signature is one of the undifferentiated squiggles the volume's note on the text says the editors interpreted 'to the best of their ability'; they read it 'Yours', and the manuscript does not settle it, so the printed reading stands.
